title: sdk: unify auth/retries & streaming ergonomics across python/ts/go, bump v1.163.0
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Unify SDK behavior for auth, retries, and streaming across Python/TypeScript/Go; ergonomics improvements and version bumps to v1.163.0. No breaking changes expected.
description:
Context: We maintain three official SDKs (python/typescript/go) and there have been subtle behavioral differences around auth refresh, retry backoff semantics, and streaming APIs. This causes downstream parity drift and operator confusion when debugging production issues. This PR unifies core auth/retries/streaming ergonomics and performs a coordinated version bump to v1.163.0 across SDKs.

Summary of changes: consolidated auth token refresh logic to a shared behavior (refresh-on-401 + proactive refresh at 80% TTL), standardized retry policy (idempotent vs non-idempotent defaults, jittered exponential backoff, 5 retries for idempotent, 2 for non-idempotent), and improved streaming client ergonomics (single-call streaming helpers, consistent cancellation semantics, TypeScript & Python now expose async iterator with identical event shapes). Also: small docs/README updates, release notes generation, and test coverage additions.

Why: Aligns behavior across languages, reduces support surface, and enables us to reason about production incidents consistently. This is a follow-up to ENG-8912 (auth reliability) and ENG-9021 (streaming parity).

High-level commit list: see commit_summaries field for per-commit summaries.

Changed areas/files (high-level): see files_changed list for file-level summary. Small illustrative snippets included inline where helpful (no huge diffs).

Review & discussion highlights:
- @Sofia Ramirez requested clearer separation between transport retries and application-level retries; author extracted a TransportRetryPolicy with explicit documentation.
- @Arjun Patel noted a race condition in proactive token refresh; fixed by switching the refresh trigger to a background task guarded by an atomic boolean and adding additional unit tests.
- @Evan Brooks suggested updating the TypeScript streaming helper signatures to use async iterators instead of callbacks for consistency; updated accordingly and added migration notes.
- CI initially failed on go unit tests due to a flakey auth mock; reran after stabilizing mock and tests passed.

CI summary: all checks passed for the final run: linux-unit-tests, windows-unit-tests, go-integration, python-lint, ts-lint, e2e-streaming, release-notes-validator. One earlier run failed (go unit tests) and was addressed in commit 3.

Merge: Squash-merged into main once approvals obtained. Authors performed a canary publish of v1.163.0 to the internal registry and validated that a downstream sample app (redwood-examples/chat) had identical behavior across SDKs.

Notes for maintainers: There are compatibility shims kept for one release in python/auth/compat.py and ts/src/auth/compat.ts — planned removal in v1.164.0. If you rely on custom retry hooks, please read the updated docs under sdk/*/README.md for the new hook signatures.
